questions.question: What is GST?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** An indirect tax.**__

 
• A type of tax that is imposed on goods and services rather than on income is known as indirect tax.
 
• GST stands for Goods and Services Tax.
 
• It is an indirect tax that has replaced all the other indirect taxes such as sales tax, entertainment tax, etc.

questions.question: Which of the following is the*** not*** a small-scale industry in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Petroleum Industry.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Small scale industries are industries that are mostly spread over a small, local area and do not require large equipment or extensive manufacturing procedures in the production of a commodity.
 
• They are '**the engine of economic growth and development of the country'.**
 
• They constitute over **70-80% of total enterprises** in most of the economies.
 
• It is the** second-largest employment generating sector**, after Agriculture in India. It provides employment to around 120 million people in India.
 
• MSMEs contribute around **6-7% of the manufacturing GDP **and **24-25% of the GDP from the service sector.**
 
• It contributes around** 45%** of the overall **exports from India.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The petroleum industry is a large-scale industry**__ as it involves extensive processes of exploration, refining, transportation, and marketing.

questions.question: The Planning Commission is replaced by NITI Aayog. What is the full form of NITI?
questions.solution:
NITI Aayog is a policy instituteof the Government of India that has been created to provide plans and support to the government so as to help them achieve sustainable development goals.

It also aims at providing a platform for the union and state governments to work together as equals.

questions.question: Which of the following is known as market clearing price?
questions.solution:
Market clearing price also known as equilibrium price is the price of a commodity at which the quantity supplied is equal to the quantity demanded.

It is the price at which the producers and consumers are satisfied and the market is said to be in a state of equilibrium.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of inclusion of Directive Principles in the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
Directive principles are guidelines or directions set for framing of policies and passing of laws by the government.

These guidelines are based on the fundamental rights stated in the Constitution and thus help to establish and maintain socio-economic democracy.

questions.question: The Panchayati Raj is based on which of the principle?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the decentralization of power.

 
• Decentralization of power refers to the transfer of responsibility and authority from the central government to the local government groups.
 
• The Panchayati Raj system generally consists of three-level Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the intermediate level, and Zilla Panchayat at the district level
 
• The decentralization of Panchayati Raj is suggested by the Balwant Rai Mehta Committee, established in 1957. 
 
• The state legislature may endow the Panchayats with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government. Such a scheme may contain provisions related to Gram Panchayat work with respect to:
 
 
• the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice.
 
• the implementation of schemes for economic development and social justice as may be entrusted to them, including those in relation to the 29 matters listed in the Eleventh Schedule.
 
 
 
• The importance is the Panchayati Raj institutes in local government that plays a significant role in the development of villages.

questions.question: Who presides over the joint session of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha?
questions.solution:
Joint sessions of Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha are held to allow the two houses to consider bills together and resolve disputes. The session is summoned by the President but presided by the __**Speaker of the Lok Sabha**__.

It is the Speaker of the Lok Sabha who is responsible for conducting the proceedings in an impartial and disciplined manner.

questions.question: By which Constitutional Amendment Bill was the voting age reduced from 21 years to 18 years in India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**61st**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Constitution 61st Amendment Act, 1988 was enacted to reduce the voting age from 21 years to 18 years.
 
• Article 326 of the Constitution provides that the elections to the House of the People and to the Legislative Assembly of every State shall be on the basis of adult suffrage and the voters should not be less than 21 years of age.
 
• Keeping in view literacy, enlightenment, and political awareness among the youth, the lowering of the voting age was carried out by the amendment.
 
• Article 326 was amended to give effect to the reduced voting age of 18 years.
 
 
• The act was also ratified by the legislatures of not less than one-half of the States by resolution.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

__
 
• 59th Amendment:

 
 
• 59nd Amendment Act, 1988 of Indian Constitution empowered the Central Government to impose Emergency in Punjab__ when deemed necessary.
 
• Under the amendment, the President's rule can be extended up to three years.
 
 
 
• 52nd Amendment:
 __
 
• 52nd Amendment Act, 1985 of Indian Constitution provided provisions related to anti-defection in India__.
 
• In this amendment, articles 101, 102, 190 and 191 were changed.
 
• It laid down the process by which legislators may be disqualified on grounds of defection and inserted tenth schedule.
 
 
 
• 56th Amendment:
 __
 
• 56nd Amendment Act, 1987 of Indian Constitution conferred Statehood on Goa__ and forms a new Union Territory of Daman and Diu.
 
• Goa thus became the 25th State of the Indian Republic.

questions.question: Who among the following elects the Vice President of India?

options.text: By the members of Rajya Sabha
By the elected members of Lok Sabha
Members of Parliament and State Legislative Assemblies

questions.solution: The Vice President of India is elected by an electoral college which consists of members of both the Houses of Parliament - Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha.

questions.question: Whose absence from the Democracy makes its functioning impossible?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Political Parties**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

__
 
• Democracy refers to a system of government in which the** power lies with the citizens **who exercise this power by either *direct voting or through elected representatives.__*
 
• **Political parties** are essential for democracy as they are responsible for voicing public opinions and formulating policies. Also, they are essential for the working of parliamentary government and help in the recruitment of leaders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__** FEATURES OF DEMOCRACY**__

__
 
• In a democracy, the final*** decision-making power*** must rest with those elected by the people.__
 
• It must be based on ***free and fair election.***
 
• In a democracy, each adult citizen must have** one vote** and each vote must have** one value.**
 
• A democratic government rules within__* limits set by constitutional law and citizen's rights.*__
 
• It is a **more accountable **form of government.
 
• It allows us to correct our own mistakes.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered as a port town of Indus Valley Civilization?
questions.solution:
Lothal is a city of the Indus Valley Civilization which is located in modern day Gujarat.

It is considered a port town as according to the Archaeological Survey of India, Lothal has the world's earliest known dock which connected the city to a trade route through the Sabarmati river.

questions.question: Krishnadevaraya was the ruler of which dynasty?
questions.solution:
Krishnadevaraya was the ruler of Vijayanagara Empire and reigned from 1509-1529.

He was the third ruler of the Tuluva Dynasty.

questions.question: The details of coronation ceremony are narrated in which of the following scripture?
questions.solution:
The Rigveda is a collection of ancient Indian Vedic hymns. Aitareya Brahmana is a branch or part of the Rigveda ascribed to MahidasaAitareya.

It is divided into 8 Panchikas and the last two panchikas explain the coronation ceremony.

questions.question: Which among the following is the oldest mountain series in India?
questions.solution: The Aravali range, a hill system in north India is the oldest range of fold mountains in India as it dates back to the Precambrian Age (4600-541 million years ago).

questions.question: Indravati, Pranhita and Sabari are important tributaries of which of these rivers?
questions.solution:
__**Godavari**__ is the second longest river in India. It originates from the Brahmagiri Mountain located in Maharashtra.

It’s major tributaries are divided into left bank tributaries and right bank tributaries. Pranhita, Indravati and Sabari are the major left bank tributaries of Godavri.

questions.question: Which type of forest is appropriate for Sandalwood trees?
questions.solution:
• Sandalwood trees thrive in the tropics where the climate is warm to hot with annual rainfall.
 
• Trees in the topical deciduous forest lose their leaves in the dry season and regrow them in the rainy season.

questions.question: Which one of the following bio-reserves of India is not included in the world network of bioreserve?
questions.solution: Under the Man and Biosphere Reserve Programme developed by UNESCO, there are various internationally protected areas that are recognized as part of the World Network of Biosphere Reserves.Manas National Park has not yet been recognized as a part of this network.

questions.question: How many legs does an insect have?
questions.solution: Insects are also called hexapods as they have six legs each of which is connected to the thorax and is divided into five components.

questions.question: Insulin activates in ________.
questions.solution:
Insulin is a hormone that is responsible for regulating the level of sugar in the blood.

It is produced by the beta cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas.

questions.question: Which among the following is not related to vitamin B complex group?
questions.solution: Vitamin B complex is a group of 8 B vitamins (thiamine, riboflavin, niacin, pantothenic acid, pyridoxine, biotin, folate, and cobalamin) that are essential for the working of certain enzymes.

questions.question: Viruses are usually made of which of the following?
questions.solution:
• Viruses are mainly composed of nucleic acid and protein.
 
• The nucleic acid that is the double or single-stranded DNA or RNA forms the genetic makeup of the virus.
 
• The protective shell of viruses called the capsid is made up of proteins.
 
• Protein and Nucleic acid together called the nucleocapsid.

questions.question: "Shrubs" are woody plants generally smaller and more compact than trees Which of the following is not a shrub tree?
questions.solution: Sunflowers are neither shrubs nor herbs. They are annual plants.

questions.question: A medical procedure, during which a small sample of tissue is removed from a part of the body, is ________.
questions.solution: Biopsy is a medical test which requires the extraction of a small sample of tissues for its examination so as to determine the extent of the disease.

questions.question: Which force is responsible for the earth revolving around the sun?
questions.solution: Gravitational force is the force by virtue of which, the Sun pulls the Earth towards itself. Perpendicular to the gravitational pull, is the Earth's velocity and it is the equilibrium between the two forces that allow Earth to revolve around the Sun in a definite orbit.

questions.question: Which among the following is cryogenic engines are used?
questions.solution: Cryogenic fuels are used in the rocket technology as the extremely low temperature is essential for lifting and placing of heavier objects in space.

questions.question: During photosynthesis light energy is converted into which of the following?
questions.solution: During photosynthesis, green plants capture the light energy from the sun and use it to convert carbon dioxide, minerals and water into oxygen and energy rich organic compounds.

questions.question: What is the reason of surface tension in a liquid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Cohesive force between molecules**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Surface tension: Surface tension is a measure of the cohesive forces between liquid molecules present at the surface.​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/029fdff65472a6e507e66fe45cdd83c150ebf9f11b9f162a918eabdfc0d429c4.png] 
 
• Molecules at the surface of a liquid are partly exposed to the surrounding. The molecules at the liquid-air interface experience fewer interactions and have more energy to escape to the surrounding.
 
• Therefore, energy is required to bring molecules from the bulk of the liquid to the surface. The stronger the intermolecular interaction, the greater is the energy required to increase the surface area of a liquid.
 
• This energy is called the surface energy and is related to surface tension as
 
• 
 
​Surface tension =( surface \:energy)/(area)

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.solution:
Input devices are hardware equipments that are responsible for providing data and signals to the processing unit of a computer.

Scanner is therefore an input device.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a computer language?
questions.solution:
Computer languages also called programming languages have specific vocabulary and grammar rules which are used to instruct the computer to perform certain tasks. FORTRAN, Pascal, and COBAL are examples of programming languages.

Languages used by us for communication like English cannot be interpreted by the computer.

questions.question: What is the constituent of tear gas?
questions.solution:
• Tear gas is also known as lachrymator agent is a chemical compound that is mostly used as a weapon as it causes severe eye, respiratory and skin irritation.
 
• Chloropicrin is a constituent of tear gas and is responsible for causing irritation.

questions.question: In which process there is gain of electron?
questions.solution:
Reduction is a chemical process that involves gaining of electrons by an atom.

The atom which gains electrons is said to be reduced and the atom which donates the electrons is called the reducing agent.

questions.question: Which of the following gas is present in bio-gas?
questions.solution:
• Biogas is a mixture of gases that are produced by the decomposition of organic matter in an anaerobic environment by microorganisms.
 
• It is primarily composed of methane, carbon dioxide and trace amounts of hydrogen and nitrogen.

questions.question: Solder is an alloy made of which two metals?
questions.solution:
An alloy is a substance that is composed of two or more elements mostly metals.

Solder is an alloy of lead and tin and is used to create permanent bond between metal work pieces.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is NOT causedy by the smog?
questions.solution:
Smog is a mixture of smoke and fog which results in air pollution and causes respiratory problems.

Cancer is a disease in which the cells divide uncontrollably forming tumours. Throat cancer is cancer of the voice box and other parts of the throat. It is not caused by smog.

Smog comprises of soot, particulate matter and harmful gases which when inhaled cause respiratory distress and on prolonged exposure can lead to asthma, emphysema, and other breathing problems.

questions.question: An increase in which of the following gases leads to global warming?
questions.solution:
• Carbon dioxide is responsible for trapping heat energy from the Sun within the Earth's atmosphere by preventing the rays of the Sun from escaping into the atmosphere. 
 
• This leads to an increase in the overall temperature and this phenomenon is called global warming.

questions.question: What is the full form of "PMSBY"?
questions.solution:
Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana is a scheme that aims at increasing the number of people with insurance.

It was launched on 9th May 2015 by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

questions.question: Which of the following schemes was replaced by APY in 2015?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swavablamban Yojana**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• Atal Pension Yojana is a government-backed pension scheme for the unorganized sector which aims at increasing the number of people having any kind of pension scheme.

questions.question: Who invented Mercury Thermometer?
questions.solution:
Mercury-in-glass thermometer is an instrument that is usedfor measuring the change in temperature as the volume of mercury changes with change in temperature.

It was invented by physicist Daniel Gabriel Fahrenheit in 1714 in Amsterdam.

questions.question: The word 'Smash' is associated with which game?
questions.solution:
Smash is a type of serving shot in lawn tennis in which the player throws the ball in the air and then hits it towards the other player in the downward-direction.

It is also called an overhead shot.

questions.question: England was defeated by which of the following countries in T-20 World Cup 2016 final?
questions.solution:
The ICC World Twenty 20, 2016 was the sixth edition of the world championship that was held in India from 8th March 2016 to 3rd April 2016.

West Indies defeated England by four wickets in the Finals.

questions.question: Which of the following instruments is associated with Yehudi Menuhin?
questions.solution:
Yehudi Menuhin was an American-born violinist and conductor.

He is widely regarded as one of the greatest violinists of the 20th century.

He spent most of his career performing in Britain.

questions.question:
Which among the following is matched correctly?

(i) Bharatnatyam - Andhra Pradesh

(ii) Kuchipudi - Madya Pradesh

(iii) Kathakali - Kerala

(iv) Kathak - Tamil Nadu
questions.solution:
Kathakali is a major Indian classical dance form that was developed in Kerala in the 17th century.

Bharatnatyam, Kuchipudi, Kathak are also Indian classical dance forms but they originated in Tamil Nadu, Andra Pradesh and North India respectively.

questions.question: "Kalinga Award" is provided by which institution/organization?
questions.solution:
• Kalinga Awards are given by UNESCO to people for their contribution in the promotion and popularization of science among the society.
 
• Kalinga Prize for Popularization of Science was created in 1952.

questions.question: There were five categories in Nobel Prizes in beginning. Which among the following is the sixth which was added later?
questions.solution:
• Nobel prize is an annual award given to people who have achieved excellence in chemistry, physics, medicine, literature, peace, and economics.
 
• Initially, Nobel prizes were awarded in chemistry, physics, medicine, literature, and peace.
 
• The Nobel Prize in Economics is the latest category which was established in 1968.

questions.question: Who is the author of the book 'Life Divine'?
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Divine Life is a philosophic work by **Sri Aurobindo Ghosh**__
 
• It was published in 1939.
 
• It deals with the spiritual evolution of man.

questions.question: Dayton Accord was signed to solve the problem of _______.
questions.solution:
Dayton Accord was an agreement signedbetween Bosnia, Croatia and Serbia.

This agreement outlinesthe general guidelinesfor maintenance of Peace in Bosnia and Herzegovina.

It marked the end of war in Bosnia.

It was signed on 21st November 1995.

questions.question: The idea of 'shuttle diplomacy' is closely associated with which of the following peace agreements?
questions.solution:
Shuttle diplomacy is an act in which a third party serves as an intermediary between two parties in dispute.

This idea is mainly associated with the Middle East Peace Accord.

Middle East Peace Accord most commonly known as Camp David Accords was a bilateral treaty that was signed between Israel and Egypt on 17th September 1978.

This treaty highlighted the guidelines for maintaining peace in the Middle East.

questions.question: The National Parliamentary body of China is known as _________.
questions.solution:
• The largest parliamentary body in the world, National People's Congress is the national legislature of the People’s Republic of China.
 
• As of 2018, it has 2980 members.

questions.question: The Union Cabinet has approved the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between India and _________ for the conservation of earthquake-damaged pagodas.
questions.solution:
The MoU was signed between India and Myanmar on preservation and restoration of pagodas in Bagan damaged by earthquakes.

This MoU was approved by the Union Cabinet on August 2017.
